kept.title: Remote Code Execution via Dynamic Import Injection
kept.description: The function `mdcConfigs` in `src/templates/mdc-configs.ts` uses unsanitized user-provided input `item` from `options.configs` directly in a dynamic `import()` call. This allows an attacker to control the path of a module load.
steps_to_exploit: Identify an application using this module that allows user-controlled configuration.
Inject a path pointing to a malicious JavaScript file on the filesystem or a URL, depending on runtime environment configuration.
Trigger the `getMdcConfigs()` function to execute the malicious code during the module loading process.
kept.impact: Full server-side remote code execution (RCE) with the privileges of the application process.

kept.title: Arbitrary File Disclosure/Path Traversal in Highlighter API
kept.description: The `mdcHighlighter` template dynamically imports files based on the `shikiPath` variable, which is used in an `existsSync` check and `fs.readFile` call. If an attacker can influence the `shikiPath` configuration, they can read arbitrary files from the server.
steps_to_exploit: Determine a way to inject a directory traversal sequence into the `shikiPath` configuration option.
Point `shikiPath` to sensitive system files like `/etc/passwd` or configuration files.
Trigger the highlighter functionality to read and return the contents of the target file.
kept.impact: Confidential information leakage, potentially leading to credential exposure or full system compromise.

kept.title: Remote Code Execution via `evalInContext` in Component Props
kept.description: The `evalInContext` function in `src/runtime/components/MDCRenderer.vue` uses `destr` and object property access, but the `propsToDataRxModel` and `propsToDataRxOn` helpers execute code in the context of `documentMeta.runtimeData`. If an attacker can provide crafted input in markdown attributes, they may execute arbitrary logic.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a malicious markdown component attribute using `v-model` or `v-on` directives.
Inject a payload that interacts with the `runtimeData` or global context via property access chain.
Render the component, causing the server or client to evaluate the injected property path or function.
kept.impact: Code execution, XSS, or unauthorized access to application runtime state.

kept.title: Insecure `rehype-raw` usage allows XSS
kept.description: The parser configuration in `src/runtime/parser/options.ts` enables `allowDangerousHtml: true` and uses `rehype-raw`, which allows arbitrary HTML injection into the document. This is a common XSS vector in markdown parsers.
steps_to_exploit: Submit a markdown document containing arbitrary `
View the rendered page where the markdown content is displayed.
The browser executes the injected JavaScript code.
kept.impact: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in the user's browser, leading to session hijacking, defacement, or phishing.

kept.title: Unsafe Dynamic Import of Plugins
kept.description: The `useProcessorPlugins` utility in `src/runtime/parser/utils/plugins.ts` uses `import(/* @vite-ignore */ plugin[0])` to load remark/rehype plugins based on user configuration. If an attacker can manipulate these configuration options, they can import arbitrary modules.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker compromises the environment or configuration source to add a malicious plugin package name.
The system attempts to import the attacker's module as a markdown plugin.
The malicious module's constructor logic is executed during the parsing phase.
kept.impact: Arbitrary code execution on the server during the build or parsing process.

kept.title: Insecure Deserialization via `JSON.parse` of Query Parameters
kept.description: The `event-handler.ts` file parses `themeString` and `optionsStr` query parameters using `JSON.parse` without any schema validation. An attacker can pass deeply nested or specifically crafted JSON objects to cause performance degradation or exploit potential prototype pollution.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a large or recursive JSON object.
Send a GET request to the highlight API with the crafted JSON in the `theme` or `options` parameter.
Observe the server process high CPU usage or potential crash due to parsing overhead.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) through resource exhaustion.

kept.title: Improper Validation of Link Protocols
kept.description: The `isAnchorLinkAllowed` function in `src/runtime/parser/utils/props.ts` attempts to sanitize URLs by checking for dangerous protocols, but the logic is brittle and can potentially be bypassed by whitespace or encoding tricks.
steps_to_exploit: Submit a markdown link with a protocol such as `javascript:alert(1)` using variations like `  javascript:` or encoded characters.
If the validation logic incorrectly flags the origin check, it may permit the dangerous link.
Users clicking the link trigger the JavaScript execution in their browser.
kept.impact: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via injected anchor tags.

kept.title: Dangerous Tag Injection via Component Mapping
kept.description: The `MDCRenderer` does not explicitly forbid certain dangerous tags like `iframe` or `object` beyond a basic list. Attackers can override components to inject unintended tags if the mapping configuration is manipulated.
steps_to_exploit: Manipulate the component mapping configuration to map a common tag (e.g., `div`) to an `iframe` component.
Inject the mapped tag into the markdown content.
The renderer renders the unintended, potentially dangerous component.

kept.title: Prototype Pollution in Object Key Pick/Get Utilities
kept.description: The `get` utility in `src/runtime/utils/index.ts` uses dot notation to traverse objects without sanitizing keys. This can lead to prototype pollution if controlled keys like `__proto__` are passed.
steps_to_exploit: Identify an input path where user-controlled keys are passed to the `get` or `pick` function.
Inject a key like `__proto__.polluted`.
Observe if the global object prototype is successfully modified.
kept.impact: Potential for application-wide property modification, leading to logic bypass or DoS.

kept.title: Server-Side ReDoS in Custom CSS Cleaner
kept.description: The `cleanCSS` function in `src/runtime/highlighter/rehype.ts` uses naive string splitting and filtering which can be inefficient on large CSS blobs, combined with potential ReDoS if the input matches complex regex patterns in the highlight process.
steps_to_exploit: Submit a markdown file containing a code block with an extremely long or complex language/meta tag.
The system attempts to generate and clean a large number of CSS rules.
Observe high CPU usage.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) due to high CPU utilization.

kept.title: Information Disclosure via Debug/Dev Console Logs
kept.description: The code frequently uses `console.warn` to output sensitive configuration information and input values (e.g., in `src/runtime/parser/index.ts` and `src/runtime/highlighter/shiki.ts`) which may be visible in logs.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger specific parser errors by inputting invalid highlighter settings.
Check server logs for the output containing the potentially malformed/sensitive configuration details.
kept.impact: Exposure of internal application structure and configuration values.

kept.title: Unauthenticated Highlighter API Endpoint
kept.description: The highlight endpoint at `/api/_mdc/highlight` is unauthenticated and performs resource-intensive Shiki highlighting operations.
steps_to_exploit: Send a high volume of requests to the endpoint with heavy code content.
The server will exhaust resources attempting to highlight all provided content.
Legitimate users are denied access.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) on the application server.

kept.title: Insecure Default Configuration for Custom Tags
kept.description: The `customElements` option allows users to define custom tags, but the module provides no validation on whether these tags overlap with sensitive HTML tags or allow injection of dangerous elements.
steps_to_exploit: Configure the module to allow tags that are inherently dangerous.
Use those tags in markdown to inject unexpected functionality.
kept.impact: Potential security boundary bypass by rendering restricted HTML elements.

kept.title: Lack of CSRF Protection on API Endpoints
kept.description: The custom components and API handlers do not appear to implement CSRF tokens. If the application is used in a context with user sessions, an attacker could trigger state-changing operations.
steps_to_exploit: Host a malicious site that sends a request to the application's API endpoints (e.g., if any handler perform side effects).
If a user with an active session visits the malicious site, the request is sent with the user's cookies.
kept.impact: Unauthorized action execution on behalf of authenticated users.

kept.title: Insecure Temporary Files usage
kept.description: The `createMarkdownParser` defines a fallback directory for the `cwd` as `/tmp` when the environment is undefined or lacks a process object.
steps_to_exploit: If an attacker can control environment variables or cause a environment misconfiguration where `process.cwd` is missing.
The module might attempt to resolve files relative to `/tmp`, which could be exploited in shared environments.
kept.impact: Potential for path traversal to other files if the system is misconfigured.
